angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 4,125,501 km at 34.70 pc = 1.59 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 45238: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 28.82 +/- 0.11 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1134/S1063773712050015): 34.698 +/- 0.132 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 5.93 +/- 0.26 solar radii from Computed here, not printed by a paper: 5.93 +/- 0.26 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.59 +/- 0.07 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 28.82 +/- 0.11 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/167.1.121): 4,125,501 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 9240 +/- 220 K from Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 80007: effective temperature 9240 +/- 220 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 80007: effective temperature 9240 +/- 220 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093)
surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.16 from 2003AJ....125.1598L; the 1 published value span log g 3.16 to 3.16, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2003AJ....125.1598L)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * bet Car: spectral type A1III- (2006AJ....132..161G)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * bet Car: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * bet Car: projected rotation speed 145.7 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2011A&A...531A.143D)
